# QS-CFW-7661-91 - Quality specification - track link CFW-7661-91 (15B37)

Revision: Rev D  
Plant: P1  
Part(s): CFW-7661-91

Scope
This quality specification defines the acceptance criteria and inspection methods for the track link CFW-7661-91 (CFW-7661-91). It applies to forgings delivered to P1 and to all in-plant operations that affect final hardness, bore diameter, and forging weight. The intent is to ensure functional interchangeability and service life consistent with design requirements for the CFW-7661-91 family.

Requirements table
The table below lists the mandatory quality attributes and acceptance criteria for CFW-7661-91.

| Characteristic | Requirement | Acceptance |
|---|---:|---|
| Through-hardness | 39-42 HRC | All finished inspection points must fall within 39-42 HRC |
| Bore diameter tolerance | ±0.02 mm | Measured bores must be within nominal dimension ±0.02 mm |
| Forging weight | Maximum forging weight 28.0 kg | Any forging exceeding 28.0 kg is rejected for this part number |

Inspection method
Hardness
- Purpose: Verify through-hardness distribution meets the requirement 39-42 HRC for CFW-7661-91.
- Method: Use a calibrated Rockwell hardness tester and apply the manufacturer’s standard procedure for HRC measurement on steel forgings. Measurements shall be taken at locations representative of service-critical sections including the girth area and the bore collar. For each inspected part, record the highest and lowest hardness values measured and compare to the requirement 39-42 HRC.
- Rationale: Through-hardness directly correlates with wear resistance and fatigue life in track link applications. Establishing a representative measurement practice ensures that variations from heat treatment or material chemistry are detected before assembly.

Bore diameter
- Purpose: Confirm bore concentricity and size meet functional fit for mating pins and rollers.
- Method: Measure bore diameter using a calibrated internal micrometer or plug gauge suitable for the nominal bore size. Measure along at least two orthogonal axes at the mid-length of the bore and at the bore entrances to detect taper. Record the measured values and calculate deviation from nominal. Acceptance criterion is ±0.02 mm as specified in the requirements table.
- Rationale: Bore tolerance ±0.02 mm is required to ensure proper press fit and dynamic clearance. Excess deviation can produce accelerated wear or assembly issues; undersized bores impede assembly.

Forging weight
- Purpose: Ensure forgings are within process control limits for charge weight and flash removal, and to verify material distribution.
- Method: Weigh the cleaned, de-flashed forging on a calibrated scale. Record the weight on the inspection record. Any part with weight greater than the specified maximum forging weight 28.0 kg shall be segregated and dispositioned per nonconformance handling.
- Rationale: Maximum forging weight 28.0 kg ensures compatibility with downstream handling equipment and heat-treat batch limits. Forgings above this limit indicate an out-of-control forming or trimming process.

Sampling and inspection coverage
- Inspectors shall follow production control schedules and sampling plans defined in site quality procedures. For each production lot of CFW-7661-91, maintain a minimum set of records that includes hardness readings, bore measurements, and forging weight for representative units and any units inspected 100 percent as a condition of corrective actions.

Records to keep
Maintain the following records in the document control system for each lot of CFW-7661-91:
- Hardness inspection log including part identifier, measurement locations, and values compared against 39-42 HRC.
- Bore measurement records showing measured values and confirmation of tolerance ±0.02 mm.
- Forging weight record indicating measured weight and comparison to maximum forging weight 28.0 kg.
- Heat-treatment batch record and furnace charge list as applicable.
- Nonconformance reports and dispositions when defects or out-of-tolerance conditions are found.
Records must be retained per site retention policy and must be available for review during audits and customer inquiries.

Nonconformance handling
Definition and segregation
- Any part that fails to meet the hardness requirement 39-42 HRC, the bore diameter tolerance ±0.02 mm, or that exceeds the maximum forging weight 28.0 kg is nonconforming and must be segregated immediately from conforming material.

Disposition options
- Rework: Parts with conditionally correctable defects (for example, localized machining or rework that will restore bore size within ±0.02 mm) may be permitted to undergo controlled rework after written authorization from Quality. Rework must be documented and re-inspected to the same acceptance criteria, including verification of hardness within 39-42 HRC where heat or stress relief is applied.
- Repair by engineering: Where engineering assessment determines a repair that preserves function and safety is possible, Quality must approve a repair instruction and all repaired parts must be re-inspected to the original requirements.
- Scrap: Parts that cannot be returned to conformance, including those exceeding maximum forging weight 28.0 kg or those with through-hardness outside 39-42 HRC that cannot be corrected, shall be designated scrap and processed per site scrap control procedures.

Examples
- Example A: A forging measures a bore out-of-round such that one axis lies outside ±0.02 mm while the orthogonal axis is within ±0.02 mm. The part is segregated and evaluated for repair; if a permitted machining operation can restore the bore to within ±0.02 mm without altering hardness in relation to 39-42 HRC, rework may be authorized and the part reinspected.
- Example B: A forging weighs greater than maximum forging weight 28.0 kg. The part is nonconforming and shall be scrapped or returned to the forge for corrective action; it may not be reintroduced to production.

Audit and corrective action
- Quality shall track occurrences of nonconformance by characteristic and require root cause analysis for repeated failures against hardness 39-42 HRC, bore tolerance ±0.02 mm, or weight exceedance 28.0 kg. Corrective actions shall be proportionate to the failure mode and documented in corrective action records.

Revision and configuration
- This specification applies to part CFW-7661-91 as identified above. Changes to the requirements must be approved through the plant configuration control process.
